name: flashhead
description: Live talking face — SoulX-FlashHead lip-syncs her persona avatar to her streaming voice, on the GPU in its own conda env
author: Teri and Chris

extra.label: Webcam packages
extra.note: pyvirtualcam: her face as a webcam (Settings > FlashHead > Webcam)

client.label: Client only
client.help: use a FlashHead server on another computer; nothing downloads here

app.label: FlashHead
app.description: Her live talking face, full size

settings.label: Between her words

options.label: Live (always moving, uses the GPU while watched)

settings.help: Loop: a few calm seconds rendered once per face and replayed, the stretch closest to her real face. Live: rendered as she sits, never repeats, and her next words flow on from where she is; the GPU works the whole time someone watches.

settings.label: Her face on her screens
settings.help: Sapphire ESP32 satellites with a screen (the Waveshare board on satellite firmware 0.7.7+) show her face: while she talks, or always (her idle loop at 2 fps between replies). A board stays a speaker first; nothing else on it changes.

settings.label: Persona face
settings.help: Empty: the avatar of the persona in the chat she speaks in, so the face follows whoever is talking. A persona's name pins that one. An uploaded face (Faces tab) wins over both.

settings.label: Her face as a webcam
settings.help: Her live face as a camera a call or a stream can pick (Zoom, Meet, Discord, OBS). Windows: the camera is OBS Studio's (install OBS 26+, keep its own Start Virtual Camera off), named OBS Virtual Camera. Linux: a v4l2loopback device. While it is on her face renders all the time: cheap with the calm loop, the GPU busy with Live.

settings.label: Her voice as a mic
settings.help: Her voice goes to the call with her face, in step. Windows: needs VB-Cable (free, vb-audio.com/Cable); pick CABLE Output as the mic in the call. Linux: a mic called Sapphire Voice appears. While on, her voice plays nowhere else unless you also turn on Hear her here.

settings.label: Hear her here too
settings.help: Her voice on this computer's speakers as well as in the call.

settings.label: Camera device
settings.help: Linux: a v4l2loopback device such as /dev/video3. Windows: leave empty.

settings.label: Mic device
settings.help: An output device her voice is played into for the call (part of its name is enough). Empty: VB-Cable's CABLE Input on Windows, a PipeWire mic of her own on Linux.

settings.label: Client only
settings.help: Use a FlashHead server on another computer instead of this one: no environment, no models, no GPU here. Saving starts or stops this computer's server.

settings.label: Pairing string from the GPU computer
settings.help: Its pairing string: on that computer, Settings > FlashHead > Advanced, turn on Share this GPU, then Add a computer (or flashhead-server's add command). Her face here is sent there; her words go there and come back with her face.

settings.label: Share this GPU with other computers
settings.help: Other Sapphires on your network use this computer's FlashHead, each with her own face, through an encrypted door with a key per computer (add them below). One GPU: her words always go first, and two talking at the same moment need a fast card (one at a time keeps up on a 5060 Ti). Saving restarts the service.

settings.label: Share port
settings.help: Port of the encrypted door other computers come in through. Saving restarts the service.

settings.label: Server port
settings.help: Local port for the FlashHead model server. Saving restarts the service.

settings.label: Models folder
settings.help: Where her models (about 8 GB) download to and load from. Empty: user/models/flashhead, which Sapphire's backups always skip (they download again if lost). Point it at a folder you already have (holding SoulX-FlashHead-1_3B and wav2vec2-base-960h) to use those, or at an empty one on another drive and they download there. A folder elsewhere inside user/ would be backed up. Saving restarts the service.

settings.label: Test the install without a GPU
settings.help: For a machine with no NVIDIA GPU (a VM): fetch the engine and models (~8 GB) and import the engine anyway, then say whether every step worked. It never renders. Saving restarts the service.
